pageCache.pageTitle: Landon School Harmondsworth - Outstanding Independent Special School
pageCache.text:
Landon School Harmondsworth
"Safe, Happy, Learning"
About Us
Landon School Harmondsworth provides education for autistic children. It supports students in achieving the goal of leading a happy and full, independent adult life. Landon School Harmondsworth believes passionately that every child has the right to maximise their potential, irrespective of their starting point in life.
Lunch Menu
Message from the Head
Jody Tranter – MA NPQH
A very warm welcome to Landon School, Harmondsworth.
Landon School is a specialist independent setting for children and young people with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs), and we specialise in young people with Autism and Severe Learning Difficulties. At Landon, we place every learner at the heart of our practice, celebrating their individuality and supporting them to thrive both within and beyond the classroom.
Our vision is clear: to create a safe, nurturing, and ambitious environment where pupils are valued for who they are and challenged to achieve their very best. Everything we do is underpinned by our simple but powerful ethos: Safe, Happy, Learning. These three words capture our belief that children learn best when they feel secure, when they are valued and supported, and when their education is engaging, meaningful, and inspiring.
A defining feature of Landon School is our multi-disciplinary approach. Alongside highly skilled teachers and support staff, pupils benefit from input from therapists and external specialists. Together, we provide a holistic programme that develops core skills for independence, communication, and personal growth.
Although still a young school, Landon has already established a strong foundation built on care, consistency, and collaboration. Our curriculum is tailored to the needs of our young people, founded on expert ​practice and research-based approaches that we use to support our learners to overcome their challenges and achieve their full potential.
We are proud of our pupils and families, who are central to our journey, and of our staff, whose dedication ensures that Landon is a place where children feel safe, respected, and inspired to succeed.
If you are exploring whether Landon School might be the right fit for your child, I encourage you to connect with your local authority SEND team and ask them to consult with us. We would be delighted to discuss how we can support your child to achieve their potential.
It is a privilege to join Landon School as Headteacher. I am excited to work with our community as we continue to build and grow a school that truly makes a difference in the lives of young people and their families.
Jody Tranter MA NPQH Headteacher

Ethos & Aims
Ethos
Landon School Harmondsworth seeks to improve continuously, innovating with best educational practice. We wish to be recognised as a leading specialist school in the UK by providing each student with the best possible life that they can lead.
Values
Aims
To educate 5-18 year old children with Autism and/or Severe Learning Difficulties so they can reach their maximum potential, irrespective of their starting point in life. We aim to support our children on their journey to a safe and happy life.

'What matters to the learner'
Personalised Learning
At Landon School, we believe that what matters to the learner – Sissons, M. (2018), must be fundamental when planning for our learners.
Our curriculum is based on a deep understanding of what the individual learner needs are.
Within the context of an underlying approach, all pupils are planned for and taught at Landon School in a highly personalised way, using developmental Personalised Learning Plans (PLPs) facilitated through an environmental context established by individual Engagement Profiles.
'Engagement Comes First'
While engagement alone is not sufficient, it is essential and a prerequisite for learning. We aim to foster high levels of engagement by:
Active, not passive, learners
Engaging in activities because they want to take part on them
The learner at the centre
of their education by considering their preferences and priorities at this point in their lives
Intrinsic motivations
Working because they enjoy the process
‘We must not only answer the question of WHAT learning should take place, but crucially, we must also pay the closest attention to the questions of HOW it should happen and, even more importantly, WHY it should happen’
Imray, Kossyvaki and Sissons, (2024)
Individualizing Learning Process
Based on Waller, J. (2024)
Personalised Learning Plans
Each child at Landon School experiences developmental challenges in a different way.
We adopt a highly personalized approach to planning and teaching, utilizing developmental Personalised Learning Plans (PLPs). These plans are carefully designed to integrate and align with various educational, therapeutic, and curriculum documents.
Each Personalized Learning Plan (PLP) is directly linked to the student’s Education, Health, and Care Plan (EHCP), ensuring a cohesive connection that aligns their education with their individual aspirations.
Engagement Profile
Each learner attending Landon School, has an Engagement Profile that aims to provide comfort, security, stimulation and motivation in any situation (Imray, Kossyvaki and Sissons, 2024).
This document offers a live picture of a learner’s engagement and motivators, serving as the first step towards a genuinely individualized planning process.
Qualitative recordings of pupil engagement in all areas of the Engagement Model (Standards & Testing Agency 2020) are made regularly on the Engagement Profiles and used to build up a picture of how developed each of these is for each pupil.
“Without engagement, there is no deep learning, effective teaching, meaningful outcome, real attainment or quality progress”
Carpenter, B. (2010)
A Therapeutical Approach
Speech & Language
Speech and language therapy empowers autistic learners to improve their communication abilities, fostering meaningful connections and reducing frustration.
Occupational Therapy
Occupational therapy, on the other hand, aids in enhancing their fine and gross motor skills, sensory processing, and self-regulation, enabling them to participate more effectively in daily routines and activities.

pageCache.pageTitle: Leadership Team & Advisory Board - Landon School Harmondsworth
pageCache.text:
Leadership Team & Advisory Board
Leadership Team
Jody Tranter
Previous Headteacher of another Ofsted 'Outstanding' school, 20+ years in education and 10 years in school leadership.
Molly Haines
Molly brings experience of specialist SEN settings and passion for supporting the development of outstanding teachers and teaching to maximise pupils engagement.
Jarka Sekhon
School Business Manager
Jarka has years of experience in business management, alongside being an integral part of operations at another Ofsted "Outstanding' rated SEN school.
Advisory Board
Katie Thompson
Katie is a legal professional working with Irwin Mitchell LLP in the London and Home Counties area. Having completed a law degree and the subsequent LPC, she is able to provide direction and support on ensuring that Landon School keeps within it’s legal and regulatory parameters
David Ward
David has over 38 years of leadership experience in schools, including roles as Headmaster at multiple institutions. He now works as a consultant supporting schools globally.
John Southworth
John is a former Chair of the Independent Schools Association and before moving into semi-retirement was as Principal of MPW London. John is a Governor of Highfield Priory School and chairs its Education and Compliance Committee and is the Strategic Adviser and Board member of SchoolTV. John supports schools on compliance and wellbeing.
Andrew Thompson
Andrew has significant CEO experience and over 15 years of educational investment and supervision experience across Europe. He owns and leads Amesbury Education Ltd, which operates multiple educational institutions including Landon School in the UK and international schools in Hungary. For six years, Andrew supervised the American School of Barcelona, a 1000-student international independent school. His extensive background in educational leadership and strategic oversight brings invaluable expertise to the development and growth of Landon School.

Volunteers
We welcome volunteers at Landon School. If you are interested in volunteering at Landon School Harmondsworth, please email office@landonschool.co.uk to register your interest. Please briefly summarise the type of work you would be interested in and any relevant experience.
Due to the vulnerable and complex nature of many of our children, we have to think carefully about how volunteers can best support us. They may not always be able to work directly with children. However, please do get in touch, as it is always worth a discussion.
